scope: Investigation and recommendation only. No production runtime changes, no server deployment or native_engine.dll replacement.

matched_kernel_measurement.scope: Same process, timing thread CPU24, 50000 game ticks after 413 preparation ticks. One full untimed warmup per backend. Compile, inputs, publication, final output reads excluded. Alternating pairs; MAIR scalar Tick, native batch16 through direct C ABI; all968 lamps and logical clocks checked outside timing.
matched_kernel_measurement.native_mode: relaxed, embedded immutable ZCore Program, batch16, -O3 generic x86-64
matched_kernel_measurement.validation: 50000 ticks after 413 preparation ticks, all968 final lamp bytes and clocks match after each sample. MAIR scheduled callback counts and native logical work are stable across repetitions. A prior separate audit matched all50001 frames of800 screen lamps; that trace is not a new check of every internal state.

current_work_measurement.scope: Untimed current-semantic38 relaxed ZCore work counts; after 413 preparation ticks and Run, counters reset; 5000 game ticks in batch16. Every batch checked against uninstrumented native snapshot/pending/clock/work.

work_comparison_limits: Native counts are newly collected from a private semantic38 relaxed DLL, checked against baseline snapshots after every16-tick batch. MAIR counters come from the saved, twice-repeated instrumented5000-tick run of the same immutable reference, fixture,413 preparation ticks and post-Run reset. Counters are not CPU-time percentages. Scheduled callbacks and token moves agree exactly.

mair.compiler: Compiler.ScanBlocks stores ordinary wires outside execution nodes. WireWatch nodes cover selected observation dependencies.
mair.inputs: ReadsLevels recognizes Comparator and WireWatch. ApplyLink has an AnalogBit chosen during BuildLinks, so Boolean inputs update only a nonzero count. Sparse analog storage uses ushort counters and occupied-level masks.
mair.movement: OwnFlips concatenates fixed group transitions. WithMoveStep stores the first64 callback-step indexes in flips; ApplyFlips sets a local switched mask; RunMoveSteps uses changed-wire masks with a general fallback.
mair.publication: Ordinary wire power is derived in TakeWire/GetWirePower when dirty outputs are collected; no full ordinary-wire shape replay equivalent to strict Redpilator.
mair.scheduler: Contiguous priority/time bucket arrays, dynamically enlarged; not the same implementation/validation contract as native event slots.

rust_executor.inputs: Already separates active u32 counts from optional analog histogram slots. Runtime construction assigns two analog channels to comparators, one to wires, none to Boolean-only components. This is the existing project pattern to port into C.
rust_executor.movement: Retains full sampled dependency/history semantics and existing fixed-case/range optimization; no new standalone Rust TPS claim here.

current_native.inputs: Dense main and side16-bucket u32 histograms for every component. set_contribution, set_arranged and side-output updates maintain histogram levels even for Boolean-only receivers.
current_native.already_implemented: Embedded static tables; direct constant accessors; cached token contributions; fixed-range replay; occupied-level bitmask; conditional relaxed lazy wire refresh; batches through64; narrow IO publication.
current_native.remaining_cost: Relaxed lazy wire refresh still keeps contribution bytes, counts and histogram updates. Current movement flips are not eliminated for ordinary unwatched wires. set_token_pos uses per-node switched/changed arrays, lists, dependency scans and cleanup rather than MAIR per-plan masks.

production_runner.scope: Rust ownership, synchronous FFI batch calls, tick credit, failure-prefix/capacity handling, publication, effects and real network client. This includes more work than either isolated kernel timer.
production_runner.comparison_limit: Prior batch16 ZCore live-loop medians approximately5512TPS without publication and5408 with IO are a separate measurement. Do not subtract them from the new5813TPS direct-kernel result to claim an exact runner-overhead percentage.

layout_evidence.limit: Bucket bytes only. The Rust-channel projection is a layout calculation, not an implemented or benchmarked reduction; offset maps/alignment and lookup costs are excluded. Retain32-bit counts until stronger bounds are proved.

recommendations.action: Port the existing Rust Boolean/analog input distinction into the native lowering and update paths.
recommendations.evidence: 4637141 of 15579169 current histogram mutations are for Boolean-only receivers (29.77%). Rust already implements the desired classification; MAIR bakes AnalogBit into input records.
recommendations.implementation_scope: Start by skipping only unneeded histogram writes, retaining32-bit active counts and original per-link contributions. Classify/bake channel information at generation time to avoid repeated type lookups; evaluate sparse bucket allocation separately if an offset lookup erases the benefit.
recommendations.correctness: Main analog channels remain on wires/comparators; side analog channels on comparators. Preserve input counts, update stamps, callback order, logical operation charges, scheduled work, snapshots/reset and exact failing prefixes. Cover all old/new0..15 strengths, duplicate competing inputs and strict/relaxed circuit traces.
recommendations.status: Recommended next experiment; no throughput gain claimed or production code changed.

recommendations.action: Precompute compact movement callback membership and changed-wire masks for bounded plans, retaining the existing general fallback.
recommendations.evidence: MAIR WithMoveStep/ApplyFlips/RunMoveSteps avoid repeated per-node membership and dependency-list scans for the first64 steps. Current set_token_pos retains those arrays/scans; the prior native profile places most samples in movement/input work.
recommendations.correctness: Preserve step order, duplicate suppression, explicit piston-head routes and per-operation failure accounting; >64-step, conditional and partial-budget paths must remain correct. Do not reinterpret batch64 as64 independent or reorderable simulation ticks.
recommendations.status: Recommended after Boolean input specialization; unmeasured.

recommendations.action: Investigate a genuinely smaller execution graph for proven presentation-only wires, not blanket observer/head notification suppression.
recommendations.evidence: Current kernel still executes 4871315 flips to unwatched wires in5000 ticks. MAIR does not put ordinary wires into its execution node graph. However, native watches26166 wires versus MAIR17657 and some extra watches preserve behavior.
recommendations.correctness: Requires complete observation-dependency proof plus faithful publication, full reset/handoff and failure-prefix materialization. Strict history must remain intact; relaxed PM1/ZCore/FPU outputs must all match. Do not assume initial idle state remains idle or that current group values reconstruct partial histories.
recommendations.status: Larger compiler project. The earlier runtime deferred-histogram prototype measured only+0.20%, so repeating that branch/lookup design is not the recommendation.

deprioritized: Larger default batches: current live32 results are close to16;64 regresses on PM1. Keep16.
More generic pointer caching/restrict: recorded probes did not establish repeatable throughput gain.
Blind strict-aliasing/unchecked/ushort assumptions: full contracts must be proved; existing native32-bit counts avoid MAIR-style counter narrowing risk.
Rebuilding already-adopted level masks, fixed ranges or lazy wire refresh: those costs were already addressed.
Dropping required head/observer callbacks or Booleanizing all wire levels: saved shortcuts can match one screen while breaking PM1 or strength-sensitive behavior.

pm1_mair_limit.reason: Saved loader omits command-block entities. This PM1 run idles at577 of12070 ticks and has23 RAM-pair and136 lamp mismatches in each repetition. Its large raw TPS is not successful PM1 throughput.

validation_limits: No production optimization implemented in this investigation; no server/DLL deployment.
New paired timing covers ZCore only; no fresh PM1/FPU timing or full workspace test run.
Final lamp and clock parity does not prove MAIR has all strict Redpilator semantics.
